tasks.task: Mobilise site and establish safety framework
tasks.scope: Site induction, SWMS review, permit confirmation, emergency contact details, occupied-building interface protocol with building management and residents.
hazards: Communication breakdown with building management leading to inadequate interface controls and resident safety risk
Incomplete or unclear induction leaving workers unaware of occupied building hazards, emergency procedures, or permit conditions
Emergency contact details not accessible or incorrect, delaying response to incident
tasks.dominant_hazard: Communication breakdown with building management leading to inadequate interface controls
controls: Hold induction meeting with site supervisor, building manager, and lead worker before any site entry. Confirm permit status, emergency procedures, resident contact protocol, and scaffold handover completion.
Display emergency contact details on site noticeboard and provide laminated card to each worker — building manager, site supervisor, ambulance, project manager.
Brief all workers on occupied-building interface rules: no entry to residential areas, no noise before 8am or after 5pm, no obstruction of exit routes or common areas.
Verify White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or current equivalent) for all elevated workers before induction sign-off.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed by licensed scaffolder and on-site before any worker accesses elevated work.
Provide each resident household with notice of work dates, contact number, and expected noise levels. Obtain building manager sign-off on resident communication before work starts.
Review SWMS for this project with all workers. Each worker must sign acknowledgement of hazards, controls, and permit conditions.
Establish daily toolbox briefing — 5 minutes, start of each shift — covering weather, scaffold condition, and communication protocol with residents.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not begin any elevated work until: site supervisor, building manager, and lead worker have completed induction meeting and confirmed permit and emergency contact status

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker to access scaffold until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and countersigned by licensed scaffolder, and all workers have verified White Card and Working at Heights competency
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: emergency contact details are not accessible, incorrect, or out of date
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker cannot produce current White Card or Working at Heights competency evidence
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold handover certificate is not signed by licensed scaffolder or is missing
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Site supervisor to maintain induction register — date, worker name, White Card number, signature, and competencies verified.
Building manager to counter-sign induction register and confirm resident notification complete.
Project manager to retain all permits, certificates, SDS, and handover documents on-site for inspection.
Supervisor to conduct and record daily toolbox briefing with all on-site workers.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest (AS/NZS 1906.1) during site entry and movement
Hard hat during any movement on-site or near scaffold

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start for first week; weekly thereafter
monitoring.evidence: Induction register signed by all workers. Noticeboard photo. Worker card sighted.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold access to all balcony work areas
tasks.scope: Scaffold installation via Kiora Lane and courtyard to each balcony. Edge protection, guardrails, safe work platform, exclusion signage below scaffold. Height >4m confirmed per HRCW.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold collapse or structural failure during assembly or use
Fall from height — worker slip or step-off during scaffold erection at >4m
Drop of tools or materials from scaffold onto residents or common areas below
Inadequate edge protection or guardrail failure allowing fall through scaffold opening
Scaffold instability due to uneven ground, wind load, or insufficient bracing in courtyard location
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — scaffold collapse or structural failure during assembly or use
controls: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licensed scaffolder before any assembly starts.
Confirm ground bearing capacity and level at all base points in courtyard and Kiora Lane access routes using site engineer approval.
Install base plates and standards on level, compacted ground — no soft fill, mud, or uneven substrate permitted.
Erect scaffold to licensed scaffolder's method — do not deviate from approved design or skip tie-back points.
Install edge protection and guardrails to full height before any worker enters scaffold — minimum 1.1 m handrail, 0.45 m midway rail, 0.1 m toe board.
Verify all cross-bracing, diagonal bracing, and lateral ties are secured and tightened — no loose bolts or missing components.
Obtain handover certificate signed by licensed scaffolder confirming scaffold meets design and is safe for use before first worker access.
Install exclusion signage and barricade below scaffold — prohibit resident and public access to drop zone during assembly and use.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: ground bearing capacity is confirmed by site engineer and base locations are level and compacted
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access until: scaffold handover certificate is signed by licensed scaffolder and edge protection is fully installed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or visible movement of scaffold structure is observed during assembly or use
🛑 STOP WORK if: any guardrail, tie-back, or diagonal bracing is found loose, missing, or damaged during daily check or during work
🛑 STOP WORK if: ground subsidence, settlement, or water pooling is observed at scaffold base locations
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Assign licensed scaffolder as responsible person for scaffold design, erection sign-off, and handover — name on permit and site induction record.
Provide scaffold erection permit to all workers before assembly — confirm understanding during site induction.
tell building residents and occupants of scaffold installation dates and exclusion zone below work — post signage in common areas.
Maintain handover certificate and daily inspection records on site — available for WHS inspection.
Arrange rescue plan confirmation with site supervisor — identify rescue method and equipment before elevated work starts on scaffold.
Brief site supervisor on load limits and permitted scaffold use — no overloading or storage of materials outside design parameters.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: High-visibility vest or shirt (AS/NZS 3833 Class D or current)
Fall arrest harness and certified lanyard (AS/NZS 1891.1 or current) — required for work at leading edges above 2 m or where edge protection is incomplete

monitoring.critical_control: Licensed scaffolder or supervisor to check guardrails, ties, and bracing daily before worker access — sign inspection record.
monitoring.frequency: before each work shift on scaffold, or daily if scaffold remains in place
monitoring.evidence: Daily inspection record on site — date, time, inspector name, condition of rails and ties, any defects reported to site supervisor

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, tile bed
tasks.scope: Demolition of failed membrane, screed, and tile bed from all balconies. Silica dust control, material containment, waste segregation. Stop work if asbestos suspected; tell WHS authority.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust during membrane, screed, and tile removal — respiratory harm, silicosis risk
Asbestos disturbance if membrane or tile adhesive contains asbestos — stop work trigger
Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges or membrane removal tools
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust during membrane, screed, and tile removal
controls: Operate dust extraction with HEPA filter at point of work during all tile, screed, and membrane removal — extraction must run continuously
Barricade balcony work area to exclude residents and pedestrians — minimum 2 m exclusion zone around perimeter
Stop work immediately if any suspected asbestos material (friable membrane, loose tape, discoloured adhesive) is encountered — tell site supervisor and WHS authority; do not disturb further
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) fitted and seal-checked before each shift — upgrade to P3 if dust suppression fails or work generates visible dust
Wear eye protection— remove and clean every 30 minutes if dust accumulation reduces visibility
Wear cut-resistant gloves and hi-viz shirt or vest
Collect all broken tile and membrane fragments in sealed waste bags within exclusion zone — do not sweep or blow debris from balcony
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove first tile or break any screed until: dust suppression equipment is installed, tested, and confirmed operational; worker RPE is fitted and seal-checked; exclusion zone barriers are in place and locked off
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: suspected asbestos material (fibrous, friable, discoloured tape, or unidentified adhesive) is observed — immediately isolate area and tell WHS authority
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, dust extraction stops, or visible silica dust cloud escapes exclusion zone despite active controls
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain asbestos pre-survey report (Accredited Assessor) confirming membrane, tile adhesive, and screed composition — attach to SWMS before work start
Issue scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder — document load rating and working load limit on site notice
Issue Working at Heights permit — detail access method, fall prevention system, rescue plan, and site-specific hazards
Record all workers' White Card and Heights competency verification — file on site before mobilisation
Provide SDS for waterproofing membrane product on point of use — brief workers on cure time, wet-application hazards, and odour / ventilation requirements if membrane is being cut or ground
Brief occupied building residents 48 hours before work starts — detail noise and dust timing, site access restrictions, and complaints procedure
Arrange daily waste collection and segregation — separate tile and screed debris from membrane and adhesive waste; label all sealed bags with content and date
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (upgrade to P3 if dust suppression fails or visible dust observed)

monitoring.critical_control: Wet suppression water flow continuous; dust extraction HEPA filter flow audible and visible; worker RPE seal-check completed before shift start
monitoring.frequency: Before work starts, continuous during demolition, every 30 minutes spot-check water pressure and extraction noise
monitoring.evidence: Daily checklist signed: water pump pressure gauge reading, extraction hose connection visual check, worker RPE fit-test record, exclusion zone photo, waste bag seal and labelling, asbestos stop-work log (none encountered or actions taken if suspected)

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed,
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, per SWMS

tasks.task: Install screed and prepare substrate for tiling
tasks.scope: Cement screed application to membrane at specified falls and thickness, curing time confirmation, surface preparation for tile adhesion, damp proof check.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Chemical exposure during screed curing — fume or dust inhalation in confined or poorly ventilated balcony area
Slip hazard from wet or partially cured screed on balcony surface
Trip hazard from screed mixing plant, hoses, or material containers left on work platform
Fall from height if worker positioned on scaffold during screed application without adequate edge protection
Damp proof check failure — inadequate moisture testing leading to tile failure and rework
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip hazard from wet or partially cured screed on balcony surface
controls: Confirm membrane is dry and free of dust before screed application starts.
Mix screed in designated area away from work platform — do not mix on balcony or scaffold.
Apply screed to engineer-specified falls and thickness — verify level and slope with laser or datum before curing.
Establish wet work exclusion zone — barricade and sign screed area to restrict occupant and worker access during wet phase.
Maintain anti-slip barriers on all access routes to and from wet screed — remove only after screed reaches non-slip state.
Confirm ventilation adequate for screed curing — open all balcony windows and doors or run mechanical ventilation if enclosed.
Check membrane damp proof with moisture meter at five points — record readings and compare to product specification threshold.
Do not apply tile adhesive or tile until moisture test confirms damp proof and curing time met — minimum 7 days or per SDS.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not cure screed until: membrane substrate is confirmed dry and free of dust, and falls and thickness are verified to design specification by supervisor sign-off.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply tile adhesive or tile until: moisture meter readings at five points confirm damp proof within product specification, curing time has elapsed per SDS, and supervisor sign-off is obtained.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet screed becomes accessible to occupants or non-authorised workers despite barricade.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails or curing fumes are visible in balcony or adjacent spaces.
🛑 STOP WORK if: moisture readings exceed product specification threshold or curing time cannot be met before next trade commences.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Obtain working at heights permit signed before screed application starts — valid for duration of curing phase.
Brief all workers and occupants on wet screed slip hazard, exclusion zone, and access restrictions before work commences.
Keep SDS for screed product on point of use — review curing time and ventilation requirements before application.
Record moisture meter readings and curing time commencement in site diary — confirm date and time of sign-off before tiling trade commences.
tell building manager of wet work and exclusion zone — confirm occupant notification and access restriction confirmation.
ppe: Respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested)) if ventilation inadequate or fumes visible during curing

monitoring.critical_control: Check exclusion zone barrier integrity and occupant access restriction before and after each work session.
monitoring.frequency: before screed application, after screed placement, daily during curing phase, before moisture testing
monitoring.evidence: Site diary record of exclusion zone check, occupant notification confirmation, moisture meter readings, curing time log, supervisor sign-off on substrate readiness and damp proof confirmation

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed and prepare substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed and prepare substrate per SWMS

tasks.task: Investigate and map slab substrate and cracks
tasks.scope: Visual inspection of exposed concrete slab, crack identification and documentation, structural crack vs shrinkage assessment. Prepare for Leo and Associates inspection hold point.
hazards: Fall hazard if crack mapping undertaken on balcony without adequate fall protection or edge barriers
Trip hazard from exposed membrane edges, raised cracks, or debris on substrate
Contact with exposed concrete surfaces causing minor cut or abrasion
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall hazard if crack mapping undertaken on balcony without adequate fall protection
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses scaffold.
Install edge protection (guardrail minimum 1000 mm high) along balcony perimeter before crack mapping starts.
Check scaffold for damage, loose ties, or missing boards each shift start — do not work if defects found.
Wear harness and lanyard anchored to fixed point if working within 1 m of unprotected edge during mapping.
Clear membrane edges, raised cracks, and loose debris from work area before mapping commences.
check concrete surfaces for sharp edges or spalling — cover or grind hazardous edges before contact work.
Document crack location, orientation, width (measured in mm), and structural vs shrinkage assessment on site plan.
Brief all workers on crack classification criteria and photographic record method before inspection starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack mapping until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and edge protection is installed and checked.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold defects are found or harness anchor point is compromised or occupant access into work zone cannot be controlled.
🛑 STOP WORK if: structural crack characteristics cannot be confirmed and Leo and Associates inspection date is at risk.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain working at heights permit signed before each elevated task commences.
Record crack inspection data (location, dimensions, type, photos) and retain for structural engineer review.
tell occupants of work schedule and access restrictions in advance — maintain liaison during inspection.
Confirm noise impact on occupied spaces is acceptable and consistent with noise management plan before work starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Fall arrest harness (if required by edge proximity assessment)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and continuous during work
monitoring.evidence: visual check of guardrail integrity, scaffold tag present, harness inspection record, occupant access log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Leo and Associates check substrate and approve repair scope
tasks.scope: Structural engineer inspection of prepared balcony slab, crack mapping, moisture testing, and written approval of repair method and waterproofing system before proceeding. Hold point — no repair work until approved.
hazards: Structural assessment error or missed defects leading to inadequate repair method and future balcony failure
Site access hazard during engineer inspection — fall from height or trip hazard if not managed during inspection walkover
tasks.dominant_hazard: Structural assessment error or missed defects leading to inadequate repair method
controls: Verify Leo and Associates holds current structural engineer licence and project-specific indemnity insurance before site access.
Provide engineer with as-built drawings, previous inspection reports, and maintenance records before walkover commences.
Confirm slab surface is dry and clean with no loose material, debris, or trip hazards before engineer inspection starts.
Brief engineer on known crack locations, moisture entry points, and any movement observed by occupants.
Conduct crack mapping using crack width ruler and photograph grid; engineer to record location, width, orientation, and direction.
Perform moisture testing using carbide test or handheld moisture meter at minimum five locations across slab; document results on plan.
Isolate inspection area from occupants and prevent access during walkover; post 'Inspection in Progress' sign at balcony entry.
Engineer to verify substrate condition against repair method proposed; confirm waterproofing system is compatible with slab moisture state.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed with repair work until: Leo and Associates written approval letter is received, signed, and filed, confirming substrate condition and repair method are approved
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: moisture test results exceed manufacturer's maximum application moisture limit for selected waterproofing system
🛑 STOP WORK if: crack mapping reveals structural movement, deflection, or signs of load failure beyond scope of surface repair
🛑 STOP WORK if: engineer identifies substrate condition incompatible with proposed repair method and written approval cannot be issued
admin: Obtain occupant consent before scheduling inspection; tell residents of inspection date and time minimum 48 hours ahead.
make sure engineer inspection is documented with date, time, photos, crack map, moisture test results, and signed approval letter.
Store approval letter in project QA file and provide copy to supervisor before repair work starts.
If moisture exceeds safe application limit, obtain written advice from waterproofing product manufacturer on drying schedule or alternative system.
ppe: Safety helmet (hard hat) — mandatory for all site personnel during inspection
steel-capped footwear— mandatory on balcony surface

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer written approval letter is present, signed, and filed before repair stage starts
monitoring.frequency: before repair work starts
monitoring.evidence: Approval letter filed in QA register with date received and supervisor sign-off

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

tasks.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to slab
tasks.scope: Installation of specified waterproofing membrane (liquid or sheet) per manufacturer and engineer specification, complete coverage of all balcony surfaces, edge detail sealing, penetration protection.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of volatile organic compounds or solvent fumes from liquid membrane application
Chemical burn or skin sensitisation from contact with membrane product or primer
Trip hazard from scaffold, mixing equipment, or membrane containers on balcony work platform
Membrane pooling or ponding if application does not follow specified falls, creating water trap and future failure
Fall from height during application if worker positioned on scaffold edge without adequate restraint
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of volatile organic compounds or solvent fumes from liquid membrane application
controls: Obtain Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for membrane product and primer on point of use before any application work starts.
Confirm substrate is clean, dry, and free of contaminants per manufacturer specification before membrane application commences.
Establish active ventilation or natural wind flow across balcony during and for 30 minutes after liquid membrane application.
Prohibit application if wind speed exceeds 5 m/s or if rain or temperatures fall outside manufacturer's specified window.
Apply membrane in thin, uniform coats following specified falls to prevent pooling; check all areas for ponding before cure.
Barricade balcony perimeter with exclusion signage during application and cure period; restrict access to workers only.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile minimum — check SDS for upgrade requirement) and eye protection
Install edge protection and maintain harness-off anchor points on scaffold before elevated application work starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: substrate sign-off received from supervising waterproofing tradesperson and weather forecast confirms application window will not be exceeded.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow occupied access to balcony until: membrane has fully cured per manufacturer specification and slab surfaces are certified hazard-free by supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation cannot be maintained, wind speed exceeds 5 m/s, or rain forecast within cure period.
🛑 STOP WORK if: pooling or ponding is observed on any slab surface or if substrate contaminant condition changes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker positioning or harness compliance cannot be confirmed or if scaffold integrity is compromised.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Verify scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder and handover certificate issued before any worker accesses scaffold.
Confirm working-at-heights permit issued and current for elevated balcony work.
Conduct SDS toolbox talk with all workers before first application; record attendance.
tell building occupants of application schedule, exclusion zone, and estimated cure period.
Maintain SDS on site and accessible to all workers.
Record substrate condition, weather conditions, application start/finish times, and any pooling or defects in site diary.
ppe: Respiratory protection — type determined by SDS volatility rating and ventilation adequacy; minimum P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested), upgrade to cartridge respirator if SDS specifies organic vapour hazard.
High-visibility vest with harness attachment point.
Lightweight glue-on or quick-dry apron if splashing anticipated.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify active ventilation across balcony and monitor wind speed continuously during application.
monitoring.who: Supervisor on balcony during application; workers applying membrane.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during application and 30 minutes post-application.
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor visual assessment of air movement; wind speed logged on site diary; SDS retained on point of use; substrate condition photos taken pre-application.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Apply new waterproofing membrane system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply new waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

tasks.task: Retile balconies and seal tile joints
tasks.scope: Tile bed and adhesive installation, tile placement and spacing, joint grouting, sealant application to movement joints and penetrations, finish curing
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of grout or sealant dust during joint preparation and grouting
Chemical burn or skin contact from grout, adhesive, or sealant products
Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges during handling and placement
Trip hazard from tile materials, tools, buckets, or grout residue on balcony platform
Fall from height if worker positioned on scaffold edge during high-level tile installation without edge protection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges during handling and placement
controls: Wear cut-resistant gloves (minimum EN388 level 3) when handling and placing tiles.
Score and snap tiles on cutting board with tile cutter — do not hand-break or dry-cut edges.
Wet-cut any tiles requiring angled or curved edges using wet saw with continuous water suppression.
Stack cut tiles upright in edge-protected containers immediately after cutting.
Clear tile dust and offcuts from work platform between each task — no dry sweeping.
Damp-wipe grout residue from balcony platform using sponge and water bucket before it hardens.
check grout, adhesive, and sealant SDS on point of use before opening products.
Mix adhesive and grout in ventilated area — do not allow dust to drift toward occupied spaces below.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile bed and adhesive installation until: licensed scaffolder has signed handover certificate and working-at-heights permit is visible on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant until: tile grout has fully cured (minimum 48 hours) and substrate is verified dry by supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker positioned at scaffold edge without guardrail or harness system visible and tested.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or rain begins during grout or sealant application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any tile handling causes cut to glove or hand — assess cause and resume only after corrective action confirmed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm working-at-heights permit is signed and posted on site before first worker ascends scaffold.
Brief all workers on tile cutting method, sharp-edge hazard, and no-dry-cutting rule before task starts.
Provide waste bin for tile offcuts — position away from balcony edge and make sure daily removal.
Record SDS product details and curing times on site notice board — confirm all users have read before use.
tell building occupants of work schedule and restrict access to affected balconies using signage and barriers.
Conduct daily pre-start toolbox talk on tile hazards, wind limits, and sealant cure windows — document attendance.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Respiratory mask (P2 minimum) when mixing grout or sealant — upgrade to P3 if dust visible
Body harness and lanyard (AS/NZS 1891.1) when working at scaffold edge over 2m

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: continuous during tile placement — spot check minimum every 30 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor observation and daily induction sign-off; document any glove damage or replacement

responsibility.SUP: Verify SDS on site, check ventilation, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Apply sealant per specification, wear PPE, report chemical exposure

tasks.task: Repair slab cracks and prepare substrate
tasks.scope: Concrete crack injection or epoxy filling per engineer approval, surface cleaning, laitance removal, priming where specified. Surface must be sound, dry, and ready for membrane application.
hazards: Inhalation of epoxy or injection resin fumes during crack repair application
Chemical burn or skin contact with epoxy, resin, or primer products
Dust inhalation during surface cleaning and laitance removal
Fall from height if worker positioned on balcony edge during cleaning near guardrail
Confined space risk if epoxy or sealant application undertaken in poorly ventilated alcove or under balustrade
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of epoxy or injection resin fumes during crack repair application
controls: Verify SDS on point of use for epoxy, resin, and primer products before work starts.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation (extraction fan or open air circulation) in work area before application commences.
Confirm substrate is dry and sound — no active moisture, no loose concrete — before epoxy or resin injection begins.
Apply epoxy or injection resin only where engineer approval is documented and on site.
Wear supplied-air respirator or PAPR fitted with organic vapour cartridge during all epoxy or resin application.
Restrict access to work area — post warning signs and barricade within 2 m radius of application zone.
Remove laitance by wet abrasion or vacuuming with dust extraction — do not use dry grinding or chipping.
Clean all surfaces with damp cloth or vacuum before priming — no dry sweeping or compressed air.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply epoxy or injection resin until: engineer approval is sighted, SDS verified on site, and continuous ventilation is running and confirmed working
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to primer or membrane prep until: substrate is signed off as sound and dry by supervisor, and laitance removal is complete
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: resin or epoxy fume odour becomes strong, worker reports dizziness or headache, or ventilation fan stops or fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate is found wet, soft, or actively leaking water, or unknown material or asbestos-suspected substrate is discovered
🛑 STOP WORK if: work is being undertaken in alcove or confined space without completed confined space permit and atmospheric test
admin: Obtain engineer approval letter or mark-up for crack injection scope before work commences.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and valid before any worker operates on scaffold or elevated platform.
Verify scaffold handover certificate is on site and all scaffolding work has been certified by licenced scaffolder.
make sure SDS for epoxy, resin, and primer is printed and available at point of use.
Brief all workers on SDS contents, resin odour warning signs, and evacuation procedure before application starts.
Keep incident register on site — record any skin contact, spill, or ventilation failure.
ppe: Supplied-air respirator (SAR) or PAPR with organic vapour cartridge during epoxy or resin application
Hard hat — maintained on site during all scaffolding work

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before application commences, continuous during work, and after each break or wind direction change
monitoring.evidence: Fan running confirmation (visual and audible), absence of strong resin odour, no worker health complaints recorded in incident register

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Reinstate balustrades and edge protection
tasks.scope: Installation of balustrade panels, handrails, and fixings per original design. make sure compliance with balcony safety standards and building code requirements.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during balustrade installation if worker is positioned at height without fall restraint or adequate edge protection in place
Incorrect balustrade installation — insufficient height, weak fixings, or non-compliant design allowing fall through or over railing
Tool drop or fastener drop from height onto residents or common areas below during balustrade fixing
Mechanical injury from power tools used in balustrade installation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during balustrade installation if worker is positioned at height without fall restraint
controls: Verify balustrade design and fixings meet original specification and Building Code before installation starts.
Erect and tag scaffold per permit. Confirm handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before worker access.
Wear full body harness anchored to independent point above head height. Check anchor before each use.
Establish exclusion zone below work area. Barricade and post 'No entry' signs. Brief all occupants before work starts.
Install debris netting or catch platform to prevent tool or fastener drop onto residents or common areas.
Use only power tools with two-hand operation or dead-man switch. Check leads and plug for damage before use.
Fix balustrade panels vertically first. Secure all fixings to full design torque using calibrated driver or torque wrench.
Test completed balustrade section — apply 1.1 kN horizontal force at mid-rail height. Do not proceed if deflection exceeds 12 mm or fixings loosen.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position worker at height until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and edge protection is confirmed complete or certified temporary edge protection is installed.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit public access to work area until: balustrade section is fully fixed, tested, and certified compliant.

hazards: Inhalation of silica dust during membrane, screed, and tile removal — respiratory harm, silicosis risk
Asbestos disturbance if membrane or tile adhesive contains asbestos — stop work trigger
Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges or membrane removal tools
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust during membrane, screed, and tile removal
controls: Operate dust extraction with HEPA filter at point of work during all tile, screed, and membrane removal — extraction must run continuously
Barricade balcony work area to exclude residents and pedestrians — minimum 2 m exclusion zone around perimeter
Stop work immediately if any suspected asbestos material (friable membrane, loose tape, discoloured adhesive) is encountered — tell site supervisor and WHS authority; do not disturb further
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) fitted and seal-checked before each shift — upgrade to P3 if dust suppression fails or work generates visible dust
Wear eye protection— remove and clean every 30 minutes if dust accumulation reduces visibility
Wear cut-resistant gloves and hi-viz shirt or vest
Collect all broken tile and membrane fragments in sealed waste bags within exclusion zone — do not sweep or blow debris from balcony
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove first tile or break any screed until: dust suppression equipment is installed, tested, and confirmed operational; worker RPE is fitted and seal-checked; exclusion zone barriers are in place and locked off
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: suspected asbestos material (fibrous, friable, discoloured tape, or unidentified adhesive) is observed — immediately isolate area and tell WHS authority
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails, dust extraction stops, or visible silica dust cloud escapes exclusion zone despite active controls
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain asbestos pre-survey report (Accredited Assessor) confirming membrane, tile adhesive, and screed composition — attach to SWMS before work start
Issue scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder — document load rating and working load limit on site notice
Issue Working at Heights permit — detail access method, fall prevention system, rescue plan, and site-specific hazards
Record all workers' White Card and Heights competency verification — file on site before mobilisation
Provide SDS for waterproofing membrane product on point of use — brief workers on cure time, wet-application hazards, and odour / ventilation requirements if membrane is being cut or ground
Brief occupied building residents 48 hours before work starts — detail noise and dust timing, site access restrictions, and complaints procedure
Arrange daily waste collection and segregation — separate tile and screed debris from membrane and adhesive waste; label all sealed bags with content and date
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (upgrade to P3 if dust suppression fails or visible dust observed)

monitoring.critical_control: Wet suppression water flow continuous; dust extraction HEPA filter flow audible and visible; worker RPE seal-check completed before shift start
monitoring.frequency: Before work starts, continuous during demolition, every 30 minutes spot-check water pressure and extraction noise
monitoring.evidence: Daily checklist signed: water pump pressure gauge reading, extraction hose connection visual check, worker RPE fit-test record, exclusion zone photo, waste bag seal and labelling, asbestos stop-work log (none encountered or actions taken if suspected)

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed,
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Investigate and map slab substrate and cracks
task_blocks_raw.scope: Visual inspection of exposed concrete slab, crack identification and documentation, structural crack vs shrinkage assessment. Prepare for Leo and Associates inspection hold point.
hazards: Fall hazard if crack mapping undertaken on balcony without adequate fall protection or edge barriers
Trip hazard from exposed membrane edges, raised cracks, or debris on substrate
Contact with exposed concrete surfaces causing minor cut or abrasion
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall hazard if crack mapping undertaken on balcony without adequate fall protection
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses scaffold.
Install edge protection (guardrail minimum 1000 mm high) along balcony perimeter before crack mapping starts.
Check scaffold for damage, loose ties, or missing boards each shift start — do not work if defects found.
Wear harness and lanyard anchored to fixed point if working within 1 m of unprotected edge during mapping.
Clear membrane edges, raised cracks, and loose debris from work area before mapping commences.
check concrete surfaces for sharp edges or spalling — cover or grind hazardous edges before contact work.
Document crack location, orientation, width (measured in mm), and structural vs shrinkage assessment on site plan.
Brief all workers on crack classification criteria and photographic record method before inspection starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack mapping until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and edge protection is installed and checked.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold defects are found or harness anchor point is compromised or occupant access into work zone cannot be controlled.
🛑 STOP WORK if: structural crack characteristics cannot be confirmed and Leo and Associates inspection date is at risk.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain working at heights permit signed before each elevated task commences.
Record crack inspection data (location, dimensions, type, photos) and retain for structural engineer review.
tell occupants of work schedule and access restrictions in advance — maintain liaison during inspection.
Confirm noise impact on occupied spaces is acceptable and consistent with noise management plan before work starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Fall arrest harness (if required by edge proximity assessment)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and continuous during work
monitoring.evidence: visual check of guardrail integrity, scaffold tag present, harness inspection record, occupant access log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Leo and Associates check substrate and approve repair scope
task_blocks_raw.scope: Structural engineer inspection of prepared balcony slab, crack mapping, moisture testing, and written approval of repair method and waterproofing system before proceeding. Hold point — no repair work until approved.
hazards: Structural assessment error or missed defects leading to inadequate repair method and future balcony failure
Site access hazard during engineer inspection — fall from height or trip hazard if not managed during inspection walkover
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Structural assessment error or missed defects leading to inadequate repair method
controls: Verify Leo and Associates holds current structural engineer licence and project-specific indemnity insurance before site access.
Provide engineer with as-built drawings, previous inspection reports, and maintenance records before walkover commences.
Confirm slab surface is dry and clean with no loose material, debris, or trip hazards before engineer inspection starts.
Brief engineer on known crack locations, moisture entry points, and any movement observed by occupants.
Conduct crack mapping using crack width ruler and photograph grid; engineer to record location, width, orientation, and direction.
Perform moisture testing using carbide test or handheld moisture meter at minimum five locations across slab; document results on plan.
Isolate inspection area from occupants and prevent access during walkover; post 'Inspection in Progress' sign at balcony entry.
Engineer to verify substrate condition against repair method proposed; confirm waterproofing system is compatible with slab moisture state.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed with repair work until: Leo and Associates written approval letter is received, signed, and filed, confirming substrate condition and repair method are approved
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: moisture test results exceed manufacturer's maximum application moisture limit for selected waterproofing system
🛑 STOP WORK if: crack mapping reveals structural movement, deflection, or signs of load failure beyond scope of surface repair
🛑 STOP WORK if: engineer identifies substrate condition incompatible with proposed repair method and written approval cannot be issued
admin: Obtain occupant consent before scheduling inspection; tell residents of inspection date and time minimum 48 hours ahead.
make sure engineer inspection is documented with date, time, photos, crack map, moisture test results, and signed approval letter.
Store approval letter in project QA file and provide copy to supervisor before repair work starts.
If moisture exceeds safe application limit, obtain written advice from waterproofing product manufacturer on drying schedule or alternative system.
ppe: Safety helmet (hard hat) — mandatory for all site personnel during inspection
steel-capped footwear— mandatory on balcony surface

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer written approval letter is present, signed, and filed before repair stage starts
monitoring.frequency: before repair work starts
monitoring.evidence: Approval letter filed in QA register with date received and supervisor sign-off

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

task_blocks_raw.task: Repair slab cracks and prepare substrate
task_blocks_raw.scope: Concrete crack injection or epoxy filling per engineer approval, surface cleaning, laitance removal, priming where specified. Surface must be sound, dry, and ready for membrane application.
hazards: Inhalation of epoxy or injection resin fumes during crack repair application
Chemical burn or skin contact with epoxy, resin, or primer products
Dust inhalation during surface cleaning and laitance removal
Fall from height if worker positioned on balcony edge during cleaning near guardrail
Confined space risk if epoxy or sealant application undertaken in poorly ventilated alcove or under balustrade
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of epoxy or injection resin fumes during crack repair application
controls: Verify SDS on point of use for epoxy, resin, and primer products before work starts.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation (extraction fan or open air circulation) in work area before application commences.
Confirm substrate is dry and sound — no active moisture, no loose concrete — before epoxy or resin injection begins.
Apply epoxy or injection resin only where engineer approval is documented and on site.
Wear supplied-air respirator or PAPR fitted with organic vapour cartridge during all epoxy or resin application.
Restrict access to work area — post warning signs and barricade within 2 m radius of application zone.
Remove laitance by wet abrasion or vacuuming with dust extraction — do not use dry grinding or chipping.
Clean all surfaces with damp cloth or vacuum before priming — no dry sweeping or compressed air.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply epoxy or injection resin until: engineer approval is sighted, SDS verified on site, and continuous ventilation is running and confirmed working
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to primer or membrane prep until: substrate is signed off as sound and dry by supervisor, and laitance removal is complete
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: resin or epoxy fume odour becomes strong, worker reports dizziness or headache, or ventilation fan stops or fails
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate is found wet, soft, or actively leaking water, or unknown material or asbestos-suspected substrate is discovered
🛑 STOP WORK if: work is being undertaken in alcove or confined space without completed confined space permit and atmospheric test
admin: Obtain engineer approval letter or mark-up for crack injection scope before work commences.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and valid before any worker operates on scaffold or elevated platform.
Verify scaffold handover certificate is on site and all scaffolding work has been certified by licenced scaffolder.
make sure SDS for epoxy, resin, and primer is printed and available at point of use.
Brief all workers on SDS contents, resin odour warning signs, and evacuation procedure before application starts.
Keep incident register on site — record any skin contact, spill, or ventilation failure.
ppe: Supplied-air respirator (SAR) or PAPR with organic vapour cartridge during epoxy or resin application
Hard hat — maintained on site during all scaffolding work

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before application commences, continuous during work, and after each break or wind direction change
monitoring.evidence: Fan running confirmation (visual and audible), absence of strong resin odour, no worker health complaints recorded in incident register

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to slab
task_blocks_raw.scope: Installation of specified waterproofing membrane (liquid or sheet) per manufacturer and engineer specification, complete coverage of all balcony surfaces, edge detail sealing, penetration protection.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of volatile organic compounds or solvent fumes from liquid membrane application
Chemical burn or skin sensitisation from contact with membrane product or primer
Trip hazard from scaffold, mixing equipment, or membrane containers on balcony work platform
Membrane pooling or ponding if application does not follow specified falls, creating water trap and future failure
Fall from height during application if worker positioned on scaffold edge without adequate restraint
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of volatile organic compounds or solvent fumes from liquid membrane application
controls: Obtain Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for membrane product and primer on point of use before any application work starts.
Confirm substrate is clean, dry, and free of contaminants per manufacturer specification before membrane application commences.
Establish active ventilation or natural wind flow across balcony during and for 30 minutes after liquid membrane application.
Prohibit application if wind speed exceeds 5 m/s or if rain or temperatures fall outside manufacturer's specified window.
Apply membrane in thin, uniform coats following specified falls to prevent pooling; check all areas for ponding before cure.
Barricade balcony perimeter with exclusion signage during application and cure period; restrict access to workers only.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile minimum — check SDS for upgrade requirement) and eye protection
Install edge protection and maintain harness-off anchor points on scaffold before elevated application work starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: substrate sign-off received from supervising waterproofing tradesperson and weather forecast confirms application window will not be exceeded.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow occupied access to balcony until: membrane has fully cured per manufacturer specification and slab surfaces are certified hazard-free by supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation cannot be maintained, wind speed exceeds 5 m/s, or rain forecast within cure period.
🛑 STOP WORK if: pooling or ponding is observed on any slab surface or if substrate contaminant condition changes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker positioning or harness compliance cannot be confirmed or if scaffold integrity is compromised.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Verify scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder and handover certificate issued before any worker accesses scaffold.
Confirm working-at-heights permit issued and current for elevated balcony work.
Conduct SDS toolbox talk with all workers before first application; record attendance.
tell building occupants of application schedule, exclusion zone, and estimated cure period.
Maintain SDS on site and accessible to all workers.
Record substrate condition, weather conditions, application start/finish times, and any pooling or defects in site diary.
ppe: Respiratory protection — type determined by SDS volatility rating and ventilation adequacy; minimum P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested), upgrade to cartridge respirator if SDS specifies organic vapour hazard.
High-visibility vest with harness attachment point.
Lightweight glue-on or quick-dry apron if splashing anticipated.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify active ventilation across balcony and monitor wind speed continuously during application.
monitoring.who: Supervisor on balcony during application; workers applying membrane.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during application and 30 minutes post-application.
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor visual assessment of air movement; wind speed logged on site diary; SDS retained on point of use; substrate condition photos taken pre-application.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Apply new waterproofing membrane system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply new waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Install screed and prepare substrate for tiling
task_blocks_raw.scope: Cement screed application to membrane at specified falls and thickness, curing time confirmation, surface preparation for tile adhesion, damp proof check.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Chemical exposure during screed curing — fume or dust inhalation in confined or poorly ventilated balcony area
Slip hazard from wet or partially cured screed on balcony surface
Trip hazard from screed mixing plant, hoses, or material containers left on work platform
Fall from height if worker positioned on scaffold during screed application without adequate edge protection
Damp proof check failure — inadequate moisture testing leading to tile failure and rework
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Slip hazard from wet or partially cured screed on balcony surface
controls: Confirm membrane is dry and free of dust before screed application starts.
Mix screed in designated area away from work platform — do not mix on balcony or scaffold.
Apply screed to engineer-specified falls and thickness — verify level and slope with laser or datum before curing.
Establish wet work exclusion zone — barricade and sign screed area to restrict occupant and worker access during wet phase.
Maintain anti-slip barriers on all access routes to and from wet screed — remove only after screed reaches non-slip state.
Confirm ventilation adequate for screed curing — open all balcony windows and doors or run mechanical ventilation if enclosed.
Check membrane damp proof with moisture meter at five points — record readings and compare to product specification threshold.
Do not apply tile adhesive or tile until moisture test confirms damp proof and curing time met — minimum 7 days or per SDS.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not cure screed until: membrane substrate is confirmed dry and free of dust, and falls and thickness are verified to design specification by supervisor sign-off.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply tile adhesive or tile until: moisture meter readings at five points confirm damp proof within product specification, curing time has elapsed per SDS, and supervisor sign-off is obtained.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet screed becomes accessible to occupants or non-authorised workers despite barricade.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails or curing fumes are visible in balcony or adjacent spaces.
🛑 STOP WORK if: moisture readings exceed product specification threshold or curing time cannot be met before next trade commences.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Obtain working at heights permit signed before screed application starts — valid for duration of curing phase.
Brief all workers and occupants on wet screed slip hazard, exclusion zone, and access restrictions before work commences.
Keep SDS for screed product on point of use — review curing time and ventilation requirements before application.
Record moisture meter readings and curing time commencement in site diary — confirm date and time of sign-off before tiling trade commences.
tell building manager of wet work and exclusion zone — confirm occupant notification and access restriction confirmation.
ppe: Respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested)) if ventilation inadequate or fumes visible during curing

monitoring.critical_control: Check exclusion zone barrier integrity and occupant access restriction before and after each work session.
monitoring.frequency: before screed application, after screed placement, daily during curing phase, before moisture testing
monitoring.evidence: Site diary record of exclusion zone check, occupant notification confirmation, moisture meter readings, curing time log, supervisor sign-off on substrate readiness and damp proof confirmation

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed and prepare substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed and prepare substrate per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Retile balconies and seal tile joints
task_blocks_raw.scope: Tile bed and adhesive installation, tile placement and spacing, joint grouting, sealant application to movement joints and penetrations, finish curing
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Inhalation of grout or sealant dust during joint preparation and grouting
Chemical burn or skin contact from grout, adhesive, or sealant products
Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges during handling and placement
Trip hazard from tile materials, tools, buckets, or grout residue on balcony platform
Fall from height if worker positioned on scaffold edge during high-level tile installation without edge protection
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Cut or laceration from sharp tile edges during handling and placement
controls: Wear cut-resistant gloves (minimum EN388 level 3) when handling and placing tiles.
Score and snap tiles on cutting board with tile cutter — do not hand-break or dry-cut edges.
Wet-cut any tiles requiring angled or curved edges using wet saw with continuous water suppression.
Stack cut tiles upright in edge-protected containers immediately after cutting.
Clear tile dust and offcuts from work platform between each task — no dry sweeping.
Damp-wipe grout residue from balcony platform using sponge and water bucket before it hardens.
check grout, adhesive, and sealant SDS on point of use before opening products.
Mix adhesive and grout in ventilated area — do not allow dust to drift toward occupied spaces below.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile bed and adhesive installation until: licensed scaffolder has signed handover certificate and working-at-heights permit is visible on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant until: tile grout has fully cured (minimum 48 hours) and substrate is verified dry by supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker positioned at scaffold edge without guardrail or harness system visible and tested.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 15 km/h or rain begins during grout or sealant application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any tile handling causes cut to glove or hand — assess cause and resume only after corrective action confirmed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm working-at-heights permit is signed and posted on site before first worker ascends scaffold.
Brief all workers on tile cutting method, sharp-edge hazard, and no-dry-cutting rule before task starts.
Provide waste bin for tile offcuts — position away from balcony edge and make sure daily removal.
Record SDS product details and curing times on site notice board — confirm all users have read before use.
tell building occupants of work schedule and restrict access to affected balconies using signage and barriers.
Conduct daily pre-start toolbox talk on tile hazards, wind limits, and sealant cure windows — document attendance.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Respiratory mask (P2 minimum) when mixing grout or sealant — upgrade to P3 if dust visible
Body harness and lanyard (AS/NZS 1891.1) when working at scaffold edge over 2m

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: continuous during tile placement — spot check minimum every 30 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor observation and daily induction sign-off; document any glove damage or replacement

responsibility.SUP: Verify SDS on site, check ventilation, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Apply sealant per specification, wear PPE, report chemical exposure

task_blocks_raw.scope: Installation of balustrade panels, handrails, and fixings per original design. make sure compliance with balcony safety standards and building code requirements.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during balustrade installation if worker is positioned at height without fall restraint or adequate edge protection in place
Incorrect balustrade installation — insufficient height, weak fixings, or non-compliant design allowing fall through or over railing
Tool drop or fastener drop from height onto residents or common areas below during balustrade fixing
Mechanical injury from power tools used in balustrade installation
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during balustrade installation if worker is positioned at height without fall restraint
controls: Verify balustrade design and fixings meet original specification and Building Code before installation starts.
Erect and tag scaffold per permit. Confirm handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before worker access.
Wear full body harness anchored to independent point above head height. Check anchor before each use.
Establish exclusion zone below work area. Barricade and post 'No entry' signs. Brief all occupants before work starts.
Install debris netting or catch platform to prevent tool or fastener drop onto residents or common areas.
Use only power tools with two-hand operation or dead-man switch. Check leads and plug for damage before use.
Fix balustrade panels vertically first. Secure all fixings to full design torque using calibrated driver or torque wrench.
Test completed balustrade section — apply 1.1 kN horizontal force at mid-rail height. Do not proceed if deflection exceeds 12 mm or fixings loosen.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not position worker at height until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and edge protection is confirmed complete or certified temporary edge protection is installed.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit public access to work area until: balustrade section is fully fixed, tested, and certified compliant.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness anchor point fails, detaches, or moves.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade fixings are loose, missing, or stripped — do not re-tighten without engineer inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached or debris netting is damaged or falls.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Provide working at heights permit signed before each elevated task commences.
Supply original balustrade design drawings and Building Code compliance certificate on site.
Brief all residents and occupants 24 hours before work. Post signage on affected balconies and common areas.
Record balustrade compliance test results and fixings torque log. File with handover documentation.
Appoint competent observer to monitor exclusion zone and occupant movement during work.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Full body harness with independent anchor line

monitoring.critical_control: Verify harness anchor point secure and independent before worker enters elevated work area.
monitoring.frequency: Before each worker access to elevated position
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of anchor attachment; tag on harness; supervisor sign-off in site log

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

task_blocks_raw.scope: Final inspection of all balcony works — waterproofing integrity, tile finish, balustrade security, cleanliness. Address defects. Handover documentation to building management.
hazards: Fall from height during final inspection if inspector positioned on balcony edge or scaffold without adequate restraint
Defect identification failure — incomplete or inaccurate final inspection allowing substandard work to be handed over
Slip hazard from wet sealant or uncured coating during inspection walkover
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Defect identification failure — incomplete or inaccurate final inspection allowing substandard work
controls: Obtain and review defect schedule and scope specification before inspection starts.
Walk balcony perimeter on stable ground or approved access platform — do not lean over or stand on edge.
Check waterproofing membrane for cracks, splits, blisters, pooling water, and substrate adhesion using visual and tactile methods.
Verify tile finish for loose tiles, grout cracking, uneven surfaces, and movement by walking and light hand pressure.
Test balustrade posts and mid-rails for lateral movement by applying firm hand pressure — no movement permitted.
Check handrails for secure fixing and continuity — no gaps in protection.
Photograph and record all defects observed — location, type, severity — on inspection checklist.
Confirm cleanliness: no construction debris, dust, or spilled materials on balcony surface or below.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not sign final inspection report until: all defects have been recorded in writing, principal or superintendent has reviewed defect list, and remediation schedule agreed or defects formally accepted as minor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: waterproofing membrane shows active water ingress, pooling, or substrate delamination affecting more than 10% of area.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balustrade posts or mid-rails exhibit movement, looseness, or separation from building face.
🛑 STOP WORK if: inspector is unable to access balcony safely without climbing, leaning over edge, or working from unstable platform.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before inspection commences.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate on site and current.
Confirm working at heights permit current and signed for this task.
Brief building management and occupants on inspection schedule and any access restrictions.
Compile final inspection report including photographs, defect register, remediation actions, and sign-off authority.
Obtain principal or superintendent sign-off on final inspection and defect resolution before handover.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Fall arrest harness and lanyard if working from scaffold at height — harness inspected for damage before use

monitoring.critical_control: Superintendent checks defect register completeness and accuracy against site conditions before sign-off approval.
monitoring.frequency: during inspection and before final sign-off
monitoring.evidence: signed and dated inspection checklist, dated photographs, defect register with remediation actions, principal approval signature

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

task_blocks_raw.scope: Scaffold removal via same access route, site clean-up, removal of all waste and temporary works, restoration of common areas, final site walkover with building management.
task_blocks_raw.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling — worker slip or step-off during deconstruction at >4m
Collapse of partially dismantled scaffold structure during removal
Drop of scaffold components onto residents, common areas, or parked vehicles during removal
Trip hazard from scaffold debris, bolts, or temporary works left on site during demobilisation
Confined space risk if scaffold is dismantled in tight courtyard access with limited egress
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling — worker slip or step-off during deconstruction
controls: Dismantle scaffold in reverse sequence to erection — top to bottom, working from safe access only, no skipping or out-of-sequence removal.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 1.5× scaffold height below and around perimeter — barricade with heavy tape, warn occupants 48h before dismantling starts.
Conduct pre-dismantle structural walk with licenced scaffolder — verify no deflection, settlement, or loose components before any removal commences.
Secure each component as it is removed — place in designated drop zone, never throw or drop components; use tag lines for loads >20kg.
Maintain harness and lanyard attached to certified anchor point during all dismantling work above 2m — no exceptions for partial loads or brief movements.
Position exclusion zone guards at base of scaffold always during dismantling — brief them on stop-work trigger (component drop, structural movement).
Clear and segregate all debris daily — remove bolts, pins, clamps, braces to secure bin before next shift or before darkness.
Check handholds and access points at each level before descending — confirm grip, footing, and handrail integrity before weight transfer.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle scaffold until: licenced scaffolder has completed pre-dismantle structural walk and confirmed no deflection, settlement, or loose components in writing.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand over site until: building management has signed off final walkover, all waste is removed, all temporary works are demobilised, and all common areas are restored.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any component falls from scaffold, strikes occupant, vehicle, or common area — isolate zone immediately and conduct full structural re-inspection before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold shows deflection, settlement, twisting, or unusual movement during dismantling — secure structure immediately and obtain engineer re-inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by occupant, vehicle, or unauthorised personnel — re-brief all parties and confirm zone before resuming dismantling.
admin: Obtain signed scaffold dismantling schedule from licenced scaffolder at least 5 working days before dismantle date.
Confirm working-at-heights permit is current and signed before elevated dismantling work starts.
Provide written occupant notice minimum 48h before dismantling commences — include start time, duration, noise levels, access impacts.
Assign site supervisor continuously on-site during all dismantling work — supervisor role distinct from guard role.
Verify all workers hold current White Card and Working at Heights competency documentation before dismantle start.
